pick.name: Cloudflare Workers (static assets + SSR)
pick.what: Static sites, SPAs and SSR apps on Cloudflare's edge, same runtime as your APIs
pick.why: Only top host whose free tier allows commercial use AND serves static assets free/unlimited; one platform with R2, Queues, Cron, Logs
pick.free_limits: Static asset requests free + unlimited; dynamic: 100k req/day, 10 ms CPU/invocation, 100 Workers/account; Paid $5/mo = 10M req + 30M CPU-ms (pricing page updated 2026-10-02)
pick.windows_fit: web + native CLI (wrangler via npm on Windows)

alts.name: Netlify Free
alts.why: Best free runner-up: easy previews and forms; credit model
alts.free_limits: 300 credits/mo (bandwidth costs 20 credits/GB, i.e. ~15 GB if nothing else); Personal $9, Pro $20

alts.name: Vercel Pro
alts.why: Pay-later pick if you want first-party Next.js features; Hobby is non-commercial only
alts.free_limits: Hobby: NON-COMMERCIAL ONLY (any payment, ads, or a paid dev counts); Pro $20/user/mo (fair-use page updated 2026-09-14)

candidates.name: Cloudflare Workers
candidates.verdict: PICK: free commercial use, unlimited static, same platform as backend

candidates.name: Cloudflare Pages
candidates.verdict: Older product; Cloudflare now steers new projects to Workers static assets

candidates.name: Netlify Free
candidates.verdict: Alt: commercial OK per Netlify staff forum, but 300-credit cap is small

candidates.name: Vercel Hobby
candidates.verdict: Rejected: non-commercial only per fair-use guidelines

candidates.name: Vercel Pro
candidates.verdict: Alt: $20/mo when you want native Next.js (ISR, image opt) without adapters

candidates.name: GitHub Pages
candidates.verdict: Rejected for products: docs forbid running an online business/SaaS on it; fine for OSS docs

candidates.name: Render static sites
candidates.verdict: Viable free static, but Render free compute is 'not for production'

decision: Cloudflare Workers wins on free commercial terms, unlimited static assets and co-location with the API, DB proxy, storage and cron. Next.js on Workers now uses vinext (beta) or OpenNext; if you hit Next.js compatibility gaps, pay for Vercel Pro ($20/mo) rather than using Hobby.
details: Cloudflare's Next.js guide (fetched today) recommends vinext (beta) with OpenNext as fallback; prefer a Vite-based framework (React Router / TanStack Start / Astro) to avoid adapter risk.

verify.note: Pricing page (updated 2026-10-02): Free 100k req/day, 10 ms CPU; static asset requests free and unlimited; Paid min $5/mo incl. 10M req + 30M CPU-ms. Limits page: 100 Workers/account Free. ToS has no non-commercial clause. See cross_issues re Next.js in final-B.
